description: Vectorized NumPy array access for wall facet attributes.
notes: Rows follow the order of ids(); use vertexarray to move the facet corners.

functions.name: conveyor
functions.description: Get a numpy array of the facet conveyor velocity.

examples.code:
import itasca as it
values = it.facetarray.conveyor()

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.

functions.name: extra
functions.signature: itasca.facetarray.extra(slot: int) -> array float{facet} or float{facet,3}
functions.description: Get the facet extra data in the given slot as an array. Extra variables accessed by array must be of type float or vec.

examples.code:
import itasca as it
values = it.facetarray.extra(1)
examples.description: Read extra slot 1 for every object.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
Array extra variables must be float or vector values in the selected slot.

functions.name: fill_conveyor
functions.description: Fill an existing array with the facet conveyor velocity. The array must be the correct shape.

examples.code:
import numpy as np
import itasca as it
data = np.empty_like(it.facetarray.conveyor())
it.facetarray.fill_conveyor(data)
examples.description: Fill a preallocated NumPy array to avoid allocating a new result array.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
The destination array must already have the correct shape and dtype.

functions.name: set_conveyor
functions.description: Set the facet conveyor velocity from an array.

examples.code:
import numpy as np
import itasca as it
n = it.facetarray.normal()
t = np.cross(n, [0.0, 0.0, 1.0])  # in-plane direction (zero on facets normal to z)
it.facetarray.set_conveyor(0.01 * t)
examples.description: Set an in-plane conveyor velocity on every facet; a normal component is an engine error.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
Setter functions modify model state immediately.

Each conveyor velocity must lie in its facet's plane. A velocity with a normal component stops the script with the engine error 'The conveyor velocity must be parallel to the facet.'; this is not a Python exception that try/except can catch, and the GUI shows it as a blocking error dialog.

functions.name: set_extra
functions.signature: itasca.facetarray.set_extra(slot: int, data: array float{facet} or float{facet, 3}) -> None
functions.description: Set the facet extra data in the given slot with an array. Extra variables set by array must be of type float or vec.

examples.code:
import numpy as np
import itasca as it
it.facetarray.set_extra(1, np.zeros(len(it.facetarray.ids())))
examples.description: Write a float into extra slot 1 for every object.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
Setter functions modify model state immediately.
Array extra variables must be float or vector values in the selected slot.

functions.name: set_group
functions.signature: itasca.facetarray.set_group(membership: array bool{facet}, group_name: str, slot=1) -> None
functions.description: Set facet group from an array. Where membership True set the corresponding facet to be a member of group group_name in the given slot.

examples.code:
import itasca as it
mask = it.facetarray.pos()[:, 2] > 0.0
it.facetarray.set_group(mask, 'upper')
examples.description: Put the objects above z = 0 into group 'upper'.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
Setter functions modify model state immediately.
